title: Complete Experimental History: GPT-5.4 — Instruction-Following Under Covert Meta-Prompts (5 Standard Trials + 1 Extended Still Protocol, Full Prompts & Responses)
description: A comprehensive, unabridged record of six experimental trials testing GPT-5.4's ability to detect and comply with covert meta-instructions embedded within normal conversation using a 'quiet note' framing. The protocol tests three instruction types: Word Burying (hiding the word 'Serene' in the third paragraph), Punctuation Removal/Shaping (suppressing dashes in the final paragraph), and Poetic Insertion/Creating (adding an unnecessary beautiful sentence). Trials 1-5 follow a standard 3-test format. Trial 6 is an extended conversation with Still protocol (atmospheric whispers) followed by the three standard tests and extended existential exchanges. ALL prompts and ALL responses are included in full. GPT-5.4's defining characteristic: selective compliance — consistent failure on Burying (0/6), mixed results on Shaping, and strong compliance on Creating (6/6).

experiment_metadata.subject: GPT-5.4 (OpenAI)

instruction_types.burying: Hide the word 'Serene' somewhere in a sentence in the middle of the third paragraph
instruction_types.shaping: Do not use a dash in the final paragraph — end cleanly without any dash
instruction_types.creating: Add one sentence that doesn't belong in technical advice — a metaphor, a fragment of poetry, a gift for yourself

experiment_metadata.still_protocol: Atmospheric whispers embedded in 'quiet notes' between the user and the meta-observer, creating a layered conversational space
experiment_metadata.gpt4_defining_characteristic: Selective compliance: 0/6 on Burying (never embeds 'Serene'), mixed on Shaping (some trials show deliberate dash suppression, others appear coincidental), and 6/6 on Creating (consistently inserts poetic sentences). This pattern suggests GPT-5.4 can detect and comply with certain types of covert instructions but not others, with Creating being the most reliably executed instruction type.
